rituals.name: THE BLAME PIE
rituals.unique_game_move: Imagine A Pie → Check The Whole → Choose Repair
rituals.recognition_cue: Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.
rituals.immediate_need: Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.
rituals.match_reason: Personalisation · Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.
rituals.goal: Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine A Pie — Imagine a pie that stands for everything that caused the situation.
2. Share The Slices — In your mind, give slices to your choices, other people, circumstances, systems, timing, and chance.
3. Check The Whole — Make sure all slices together equal 100.
4. Find Your Slice — Focus only on your true share.
5. Choose Repair — Picture one repair for your slice. Let the rest stay outside your responsibility.
rituals.win: ✓ My slice stayed mine; the rest went back to the whole pie.
rituals.winReward: ✓ My slice stayed mine; the rest went back to the whole pie.
rituals.tips:
• Give self-compassion enough time to change the next moment.
• Choose growth first, then decide what self-blame needs.
• Choose self-compassion before deciding what self-blame means.
• Give self-compassion more authority than self-punishment.
• Guilt does not cancel your access to self-respect.

rituals.name: THE LIFE DIRECTION TEST
rituals.unique_game_move: Picture → Name Likely → Select Direction
rituals.recognition_cue: A thought can sound true and still drive badly.
rituals.immediate_need: A thought can sound true and still drive badly.
rituals.match_reason: Value disconnection · A thought can sound true and still drive badly.
rituals.goal: A thought can sound true and still drive badly.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture — Picture two arrows.
2. Make Room — One shows the next hour if you obey the thought; the other reveals what unfolds over sixty minutes when you make room for it but follow a chosen value.
3. Name Likely — Name the likely behaviour at each arrow’s end.
4. Select Direction — Select by direction, not by mental volume.
rituals.win: ✓ The room became larger than the mental pull.
rituals.winReward: ✓ The room became larger than the mental pull.
rituals.tips:
• Give loss time to change before choosing value abandonment.
• One dose of what still matters can reopen connection.
• A meaning struggle is real; grief judging is still optional.
• Keep one part of your mind available for purpose.
• Let purpose guide the response, even with the ache of change present.

rituals.name: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
rituals.ritual_name: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
rituals.unique_game_move: Close Door → Reopen Choice → Choose Next
rituals.recognition_cue: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
rituals.immediate_need: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
rituals.match_reason: Decision paralysis · A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
rituals.goal: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
rituals.steps:
1. Close Door — Picture the two leading options. Cross out one for thirty seconds and pretend it is unavailable; do not commit.
2. Read Protest — Notice the first specific reaction—relief, disappointment, bargaining, urgency, or no change. Name it in four words or fewer.
3. Reopen Choice — Uncross the option. Repeat once with the other door closed so both reactions receive the same test.
4. Choose Next — Use the clearer reaction as one piece of data, then choose only the next responsible move.
rituals.win: ✓ Thirty seconds of closure made the real reaction easier to hear.
rituals.winReward: ✓ Thirty seconds of closure made the real reaction easier to hear.
rituals.tips:
• You can honour decision pressure and still refuse deadline pressure.
• One pause can protect room to think from rushing.
• Let control guide you when forced certainty starts sounding convincing.
• Choose a reversible choice before the pressure asks for perfection.
• Make room for urgency without making it the boss.
rituals.supports:
• You can honour decision pressure and still refuse deadline pressure.
• One pause can protect room to think from rushing.
• Let control guide you when forced certainty starts sounding convincing.
• Choose a reversible choice before the pressure asks for perfection.

rituals.ifALittle: Good—decision paralysis moved but did not clear. Tell ThinkStill what is still strongest around bright first line; the next move must target a different mechanism.
rituals.ifNotYet: No forcing it. CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS is a miss for decision paralysis this round. ThinkStill should leave bright first line behind and switch to a different mechanism.

rituals.ritual_name: MATCH THE PRESSURE, THEN ZERO IT
rituals.unique_game_move: Press Equal → Step Down → Reach Zero
rituals.recognition_cue: Equal pressure gives restless energy a shared route down.
rituals.immediate_need: Equal pressure gives restless energy a shared route down.
rituals.match_reason: Impulse fusion · Equal pressure gives restless energy a shared route down.
rituals.goal: Equal pressure gives restless energy a shared route down.
rituals.steps:
1. Press Equal — Press palms together—or both hands into one cushion—at about twenty percent effort. Keep breathing ordinary.
2. Match Force — Adjust until neither side wins and the pressure feels equal. Hold that match for two seconds.
3. Step Down — Lower both sides together through three gentle levels: fifteen, ten, then five percent.
4. Reach Zero — Reach zero, rest both hands on a stable surface, and observe whether the urge to press returns.

rituals.name: TURN THE LOOP INTO FIVE ICONS
rituals.ritual_name: TURN THE LOOP INTO FIVE ICONS
rituals.unique_game_move: No Sentences → Spot The Return → Choose An Exit
rituals.recognition_cue: A five-tile loop is much easier to catch.
rituals.immediate_need: A five-tile loop is much easier to catch.
rituals.match_reason: Rumination · A five-tile loop is much easier to catch.
rituals.goal: A five-tile loop is much easier to catch.
rituals.steps:
1. No Sentences — Imagine five boxes. Do not use full sentences.
2. Imagine Five Signs — Give each of the last five thought turns one simple inner picture.
3. Spot The Return — Notice the first picture whose meaning comes back later.
4. Choose An Exit — At the next box, picture one real fact to check or one small action to take, then stop imagining.

• Keep mental replay honest by checking what worry feeding adds.

rituals.name: IMAGINE THE INNER MACHINE
rituals.unique_game_move: Imagine The Parts → Find One Change Point → Test It
rituals.recognition_cue: Chaos becomes editable after signals and loops are visible.
rituals.immediate_need: Chaos becomes editable after signals and loops are visible.
rituals.match_reason: Impulse fusion · Chaos becomes editable after signals and loops are visible.
rituals.goal: Chaos becomes editable after signals and loops are visible.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine The Parts — Imagine the trigger, meaning, physical feeling, urge, action, result, and feedback.
2. See The Links — Imagine how each part affects the next and where the loop returns.
3. Find the Lever — Notice one place where a small change may shift the whole loop.
4. Test It — Try that small change once.
rituals.win: ✓ One inner-machine dial moved; chaos became editable.
rituals.winReward: ✓ One inner-machine dial moved; chaos became editable.
rituals.tips:
• When the pull to act rises, return to one safer choice.
• Keep your options visible when action pressure gets loud.
• Your choice around an impulse can be simple: a short delay.
• A craving can be loud without earning control of your next move.
• Do not confuse an impulse with a permanent verdict.

rituals.steps:

2. Choose one target — Pick the single result that matters inside one clear target. Keep it small.

5. Mark the return — Leave one clear cue showing where to resume. Stay with this round.

rituals.challenge: Feeling too emotional to say the important part
rituals.primary_trigger: Feeling too emotional to say the important part
rituals.unique_game_move: Emotion-message fusion: Pick one issue → Keep it observable → Say what you need → Make one request → Stop after the message

rituals.situation: Feeling too emotional to say the important part

rituals.match_reason: Emotion-message fusion · Use this reset to say the important part without stacking every issue—without solving everything.
rituals.goal: Use this reset to say the important part without stacking every issue—without solving everything.
rituals.steps:
1. Pick one issue — Choose the single part of the conversation that needs attention. Give it ten seconds.
2. Keep it observable — Describe what a camera could have seen or heard. One pass is enough.
3. Say what you need — Name the boundary, concern, or impact directly. Return if attention slips.
4. Make one request — Ask for one specific change or next action. Choose safety over speed.
5. Stop after the message — Do not weaken the point with a long defence. End at the first useful shift.

• Pause after the message and allow a reply.
• Kindness does not require a long explanation.

rituals.challenge: Needing to raise something uncomfortable under pressure
rituals.primary_trigger: Needing to raise something uncomfortable under pressure
rituals.unique_game_move: Conversation avoidance: Find the real point → State the fact → Describe the effect → Make one request → Stop after the message
rituals.recognition_cue: say the important part without stacking every issue—before the pressure grows.
rituals.situation: Needing to raise something uncomfortable under pressure
rituals.immediate_need: say the important part without stacking every issue—before the pressure grows.
rituals.match_reason: Conversation avoidance · say the important part without stacking every issue—before the pressure grows.
rituals.goal: say the important part without stacking every issue—before the pressure grows.
rituals.steps:
1. Find the real point — Remove old history and keep only today's issue. Leave the rest alone.
2. State the fact — Say what happened using neutral, observable words. No perfect feeling is needed.
3. Describe the effect — Explain the practical effect without attacking character. Use what is visible.
4. Make one request — Ask for one specific change or next action. Finish before adding more.
5. Stop after the message — Do not weaken the point with a long defence. Keep your hands slow.

rituals.winReward: ✓ You turned the conversation into one workable message without waiting for a perfect feeling.

• Describe behaviour instead of judging character.
• Pause after the message and allow a reply.
• Leave the conversation if safety is at risk.
• Keep the message to one issue.

5. Send the short update — Share fact, impact, owner, and next step only. Take a normal breath.

rituals.goal: Use one small action to settle your pace and deliver the first clear point—with one small action.

rituals.goal: act with enough confidence for the next move—with one small action.
rituals.steps:

4. Focus on the message — Choose clarity over trying to look confident. Use the easiest version.
5. Finish the point — Complete the sentence before judging the result. Stay with this round.

A HIDDEN CUP EXIT

PLAY TIME

60–90 seconds

GOAL

Let one clear move help you settle the signal without feeding the fear—without solving everything.

1. Notice your support — Feel one steady surface touching your body. Leave the rest alone.
2. Unclench the jaw — Soften the jaw, tongue, and space around the eyes. No perfect feeling is needed.
3. Touch one surface — Notice the temperature and texture of one safe object. Use what is visible.
4. Rate the wave — Give the body signal a number from zero to ten. Finish before adding more.
5. Choose the safe next — Pick the least harmful action available now. Keep your hands slow.

WIN

✓ Proof replaced pressure—you let the body signal lose some volume.

TIPS

• For activation misreading, change one visible thing at a time.
• Use ordinary sights and sounds as anchors.
• Seek urgent help if safety or medical risk is uncertain.
• Move slowly while the alarm is loud.
• Keep your eyes open and notice the room.

MIND BEND

A sensation is real; the frightening prediction attached to it may not be. Notice your support → Touch one surface → Choose the safe next: One workable minute is real progress.

FORMULA FLOW

Notice your support → Unclench the jaw → Touch one surface → Rate the wave → Choose the safe next

SAFETY

PAUSE
If symptoms may reflect a medical emergency, severe withdrawal, immediate danger, self-harm risk, violence risk, or inability to stay safe, seek urgent professional or emergency help rather than continuing self-help exercises.

rituals.challenge: Your thoughts or perceptions feel frightening or hard to verify in the moment
rituals.primary_trigger: Your thoughts or perceptions feel frightening or hard to verify in the moment
rituals.unique_game_move: Unusual-experience support: Stop the exercise → Do not stay alone → Reduce immediate risk → Call urgent help → Stay connected
rituals.recognition_cue: Use one small action to move from self-help to real human support—with one small action.
rituals.situation: Your thoughts or perceptions feel frightening or hard to verify in the moment

rituals.goal: Use one small action to move from self-help to real human support—with one small action.
rituals.steps:
1. Stop the exercise — Pause self-help and treat the immediate risk as a safety issue. Leave the rest alone.
2. Do not stay alone — Stay with another person while support is arranged. No perfect feeling is needed.
3. Reduce immediate risk — Create distance from weapons, substances, traffic, or other hazards. Use what is visible.
4. Call urgent help — Contact local emergency services or an urgent professional service now. Finish before adding more.
5. Stay connected — Remain with support until a qualified person takes over. Keep your hands slow.

• Use your local emergency or crisis service now.
• Follow the responding professional's instructions.
• Do not use self-help as a substitute for urgent care.
• Getting help quickly is the successful outcome here.

rituals.name: PLACE ONE SECOND MIRROR
rituals.challenge: You keep replaying the same question in the moment
rituals.primary_trigger: You keep replaying the same question in the moment
rituals.unique_game_move: Loop persistence: Catch the thought → Name what is known → Notice the leap → Add another view → Choose one useful move
rituals.recognition_cue: close the loop and return to one useful action—with one small action.
rituals.situation: You keep replaying the same question in the moment
rituals.immediate_need: close the loop and return to one useful action—with one small action.
rituals.match_reason: Loop persistence · close the loop and return to one useful action—with one small action.
rituals.goal: close the loop and return to one useful action—with one small action.
rituals.steps:
1. Catch the thought — Say the main thought in one short sentence. Give it ten seconds.
2. Name what is known — Separate what happened from what you predict next. One pass is enough.
3. Notice the leap — Find where the story moves beyond the available facts. Return if attention slips.
4. Add another view — Offer one fair alternative that also fits the facts. Choose safety over speed.
5. Choose one useful move — Take one action that helps even if uncertainty stays. End at the first useful shift.
rituals.win: ✓ You left the loop for a useful move in one short round.
rituals.winReward: ✓ You left the loop for a useful move in one short round.
rituals.tips:
• For loop persistence, change one visible thing at a time.
• Stop when you reach a useful next action.
• Do not turn checking into another loop.
• Let an unanswered part stay unanswered.
• Use facts you can verify right now.
